claims.text: Catalyst durability during ethanol oxidation is governed by the degree of atomic randomness.
Rapid quenching produces a fully or highly randomized atomic arrangement in nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalysts.
Greater atomic randomness enhances durability by optimizing multinary interactions and minimizing vulnerable deactivation sites.
Slow cooling or slow chemical reduction permits mild local atomic ordering.
Mild local ordering promotes the formation of vulnerable clusters.
Vulnerable clusters accelerate catalyst degradation under ethanol-oxidation conditions.
The initial catalyst is an equiatomic nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs solid solution synthesized by conventional chemical reduction.
EXAFS and PDF analyses can quantify the degree of local atomic order in these catalysts.
A randomized PtPdRhRuIrOs structure resists localized deactivation by preferential oxidation or dissolution.
Rapidly quenched, highly random catalysts will retain catalytic activity longer than the comparator catalysts.
Durability will correlate positively with atomic disorder measured by EXAFS and PDF.
The proposed relationship applies to nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs solid solutions during ethanol oxidation in acidic media at room temperature.
Changes in composition, synthesis-induced defects, or reaction environment may limit the proposed relationship.

contradictions.description: The comparator is not consistently defined: it is described as slow chemical reduction, slow cooling, and conventional chemical reduction with standard cooling. These are not necessarily the same treatment, so the intended baseline is ambiguous.
